Rashi on Arakhin 28a:10:1.english: One who dispenses - to the poor:

Rashi on Arakhin 28a:10:2.hebrew: חומש - דגמרינן מיעקב, דכתיב ביה תרין עישורין. ר' אלעזר בן עזריה אית ליה דרבי אילא, דהא אתא לאשמועינן שיהא אדם חס על נכסיו; ר"א לית ליה דרבי אילא, דאי בזבז טובא לא איכפת לן, אלא ששייר לעצמו קצת, דומיא דחרם:
Rashi on Arakhin 28a:10:2.english: A fifth - for we learn [this] from Jacob, regarding whom two tithes are written. Rabbi Elazar ben Azaryah holds [the view] of Rabbi Ila, for he comes to teach us that a person should spare his property; Rabbi Eliezer does not hold [the view] of Rabbi Ila, for if one dispenses a great deal we do not mind, provided that he leaves a little for himself, similar to cherem [dedicating one's property]:

Rashi on Arakhin 28a:12:1.hebrew: שהחרמים שלהם - דכתיב "כל חרם בישראל" וגו', וכיון דדידיה הוא, מה הנאה בכך? אי הוה מחרים, איהו גופיה זכי ביה ולא יהב ליה לכהן אחר:
Rashi on Arakhin 28a:12:1.english: As dedicated [property] is theirs - as it is written: "Everything dedicated in Israel [shall be yours]" (Numbers 18:14), etc., and since it is his, what benefit is there in this? If he were to dedicate [his property], he himself would acquire it and would not give it to another priest.

Rashi on Arakhin 28a:13:1.hebrew: נראין דברי ר' יהודה - דלוים אין מחרימין בקרקעות:
Rashi on Arakhin 28a:13:1.english: The statement of Rabbi Yehuda appears [correct] - that Levites do not dedicate [property] with regard to land:

Rashi on Arakhin 28a:13:2.hebrew: ודברי ר' שמעון במטלטלין - שהרי אין החרמים שלהן, הלכך אי מחרימי מטלטלין, חיילא עלייהו חרם ויהבי להו לכהנים:
Rashi on Arakhin 28a:13:2.english: And the statement of Rabbi Shimon [appears correct] with regard to movable property - for dedicated items are not theirs [i.e., the Levites']; therefore, if they dedicate movable property, the dedication takes effect upon them [those items], and they give them to the priests:

Rashi on Arakhin 28a:14:1.hebrew: מדאיצטריך ליה לרבי למימר במטלטלין נראין דברי <abbr title="רבי שמעון">ר"ש</abbr>, דמשמע אבל בקרקעות אין נראין דבריו, מכלל דאקרקעות נמי פליגי:
Rashi on Arakhin 28a:14:1.english: Since Rabbi [Yehuda HaNasi] needed to say [that] with regard to movable property the statement of Rabbi Shimon appears [correct] — which implies [that] with regard to land his statement does not appear [correct] — it follows by implication that they disagree regarding land as well:

Rashi on Arakhin 28a:16:1.hebrew: שאף רבי שמעון לא נחלק עליו כו' - והכי משמע מילתיה דרבי: נראין דברי ר' יהודה לר' שמעון בקרקעות, שדברי ר"ש במטלטלין:
Rashi on Arakhin 28a:16:1.english: As even Rabbi Shimon did not disagree with him, etc. - And this is what Rabbi [Yehuda HaNasi]'s statement means: The words of Rabbi Yehuda appear [correct] to Rabbi Shimon with regard to land, for the words of Rabbi Shimon [apply only] with regard to movable property:

Rashi on Arakhin 28a:1:1.hebrew: והיכי דמי כגון דאמרי בכ"א - דהוי בין קרן בין חומש כ"ו ודינר, וזה מוסיף ה', היינו ל"א ודינר:
Rashi on Arakhin 28a:1:1.english: And what are the circumstances? For example, where they said [they would redeem it] for twenty-one [sela] - for [the total], both principal and [the additional] fifth, is twenty-six [sela] and a dinar, and this [other person] adds five [sela], which comes to thirty-one [sela] and a dinar:

Rashi on Arakhin 28a:1:2.hebrew: הבעלים קודמין - דאי הוה יהבינן ליה להאי, הוה פסיד הקדש דינר ממאי דאמור ברישא, הלכך הדרי אבעלים על כרחייהו:
Rashi on Arakhin 28a:1:2.english: The owner takes precedence - For if we were to give it to this [other bidder], the Temple treasury would lose a dinar from what [the owner] offered initially; therefore, it reverts to the owner against his will:

Rashi on Arakhin 28a:1:3.hebrew: ואם לאו אומר לו לזה הגעתיך - דאמרי בעלים, "אתא גברא בחריקן":
Rashi on Arakhin 28a:1:3.english: And if not, he says to this one, "It has come into your [possession]" - For the owners say, "A man has come in our stead":

Rashi on Arakhin 28a:2:1.hebrew: מצאנו - מקצת צאנו, אומר "הרי הן חרם", ונותנן לכהן:
Rashi on Arakhin 28a:2:1.english: Of his flock - [meaning] part of his flock; he says, "Behold, they are cherem [dedicated]," and gives them to the priest:

Rashi on Arakhin 28a:2:2.english: All of them - [meaning] that he did not leave anything for himself:

Rashi on Arakhin 28a:2:3.english: To spare his property - [Meaning] that he should not squander it on an ordinary person:

Rashi on Arakhin 28a:3:1.hebrew: מכל אשר לו - היינו מטלטלין, ולא כל מטלטלין:
Rashi on Arakhin 28a:3:1.english: Of all that he has - this refers to movable property, and [means] not all movable property:

Rashi on Arakhin 28a:3:2.english: Of man - [this refers to] Canaanite slaves:

Rashi on Arakhin 28a:4:1.english: Notwithstanding, any devoted thing - [The terms] akhin ["notwithstanding"] and rakin ["only"] [indicate] exclusions:

Rashi on Arakhin 28a:6:1.english: By distoran - That he would be a sharecropper for others, and receive fields [to cultivate] for a half, a third, or a quarter [of the produce]:

Rashi on Arakhin 28a:6:2.hebrew: אבל מטלטלין אימא ליחרמינהו כולהו - כתב רחמנא "מכל אשר לו", ולא "כל אשר לו", דהיינו מטלטלין:
Rashi on Arakhin 28a:6:2.english: But [regarding] movable property, I would say let him dedicate all of them - The Merciful One wrote "of all that he has" and not "all that he has" — which refers to movable property:

Rashi on Arakhin 28a:8:1.hebrew: בתו - יש לו רשות למוכרה בקטנותה, ולא בנערותה:
Rashi on Arakhin 28a:8:1.english: His daughter - he has permission to sell her during her minorhood, and not during her maidenhood:

Tosafot on Arakhin 28a:17:1.hebrew: החרים מטלטלין נותנן לכל כהן שירצה שנאמר כל חרם בישראל לך יהיה - אין זה עיקר דרש, דהא קרא איצטריך כדדריש ליה לקמיה: "נתנו לכהן, הרי הוא כחולין לכל דבריו, שנאמר: כל חרם בישראל לך יהיה". והא דאמר הכא "נותנן לכל כהן שירצה", מסברא הוא, כמו תרומה שנותנה לכל כהן, ואין צריך ליתנה לכהן שבאותו משמר. ועוד, אי הוי עיקר דרשא, מאי הא דפריך לקמן "ליקיש מטלטלין לקרקעות"? והלא גזירת הכתוב היא! אלא ש"מ דלאו עיקר דרשה הוא זה:
Tosafot on Arakhin 28a:17:1.english: One who dedicated movable property may give it to any priest that he wishes, as it is stated: “Everything dedicated in Israel shall be yours” - This is not the primary exposition [of the verse], for the verse is needed as [the Gemara] expounds it later: “[Once] he has given it to the priest, it is like non-sacred property in all respects, as it is stated: ‘Everything dedicated in Israel shall be yours.’” And that which [the Gemara] says here, “he may give it to any priest that he wishes,” is based on logical reasoning, like terumah, which one may give to any priest and does not need to give it [specifically] to a priest of that [priestly] watch. Furthermore, if it were the primary exposition, what is [the meaning of] that which [the Gemara] objects later: “Let us compare movable property to land”? Surely it is a scriptural decree! Rather, learn from this that this is not the primary exposition:

Tosafot on Arakhin 28a:3:1.hebrew: דתנו רבנן מכל אשר לו ולא כל אשר לו - וא"ת: והא האי קרא בחרם הניתן לכהנים כתיב, דהא בסיפיה דקרא כתיב "לא ימכר ולא יגאל", ואילו חרמי בדק הבית יש להם פדיון כהקדש; והיכי קאמר במתני' "ומה אם לגבוה כו'", והא לאו לגבוה הוא כי אם לכהנים! ועוד, דאיכא בפרק השולח (גיטין דף לח:): "מאדם — אלו עבדיו ושפחותיו הכנענים", ופריך מינה לרב דאמר המקדיש עבדו יצא לחירות, דלמיהוי עם קדוש קאמר; ומאי קפריך? והא בחרמים אין בהן קדושת הגוף, ולא דמי למקדיש לומר דלמיהוי עם קדוש קאמר! וי"ל, דאפי' בחרמים הניתנין לכהנים יש בהן קדושת הגוף, כדתני לקמן בפירקין (ערכין דף כט.): חרמים, כל זמן שהן בבית בעלים — הרי הן כהקדש לכל דבריהם; נתנם לכהן — הרי הן כחולין. אלמא אית בהו קדושת הגוף:
Tosafot on Arakhin 28a:3:1.english: As the Sages taught: "Of all that he has," and not all that he has - And if you will ask: Surely this verse is written regarding a dedication given to the priests, for at the end of the verse it is written, "it shall not be sold and it shall not be redeemed," whereas dedications for the upkeep of the Temple have redemption like consecrated property! So how does [the Tanna] say in the Mishnah, "If for the Most High, etc." — surely it is not for the Most High, but rather for the priests! Furthermore, there is [a baraita] in the chapter [entitled] HaSholeach (Gittin 38b): "'Of man' — these are his Canaanite slaves and maidservants," and [the Gemara] raises an objection from it against Rav, who says that [if] one consecrates his slave, [the slave] goes out to freedom, because [the master] meant that he should become [part of] a holy nation. But what is [the Gemara] objecting? Surely in dedications there is no inherent sanctity, and it is not comparable to one who consecrates [a slave], to say that he meant that he should become [part of] a holy nation! And one can answer that even in dedications given to the priests there is inherent sanctity, as it is taught later in our chapter (Arakhin 29a): Dedications, as long as they are in the owner's house, are like consecrated property in all respects; [once] he gives them to the priest, they are like non-sacred property. Thus we see that they have inherent sanctity:

Tosafot on Arakhin 28a:8:1.hebrew: (אלא) [ת"ל] בהמה, מה בהמה יש לו רשות למכור לעולם - וא"ת: א"כ, שדה אחוזה נמי, שהרי אם מכרה חוזרת לבעלים ביובל? וי"ל: דמ"מ יש לו רשות להוציא מידו לעולם, כגון אם הקדישה וגאלה אחר, שמתחלקת לכהנים ביובל. א"נ י"ל דה"פ: מה בהמה יש לו רשות למוכרה — ושדה אחוזה נמי, כל זמן שהיא בידו יכול הוא למוכרה, משא"כ בבתו, דמשתגדיל אין לו רשות למוכרה:
Tosafot on Arakhin 28a:8:1.english: (Rather,) [The verse states] "animal"; just as an animal he has permission to sell forever - And if you ask: If so, [one should not be able to dedicate] an ancestral field either, since if he sells it, it returns to the [original] owners in the Jubilee [year]? One can answer that nevertheless, he has permission to remove it from his possession forever, such as if he consecrated it and another person redeemed it, in which case it is divided among the priests in the Jubilee [year]. Alternatively, one can say that this is its explanation: "Just as an animal he has permission to sell" — and an ancestral field too, as long as it is in his possession he is able to sell it — unlike his daughter, whom once she reaches majority he has no permission to sell:
